title: Cyberattack hits 178 websites, targets older Apple devices

blocks.text: MANILA, Philippines – Hackers recently targeted 178 websites with a malicious cyberattack designed to steal financial information and infect older Apple devices.
Attackers injected malware into Optimizely, a platform used by major companies such as BBC, CNN, IKEA, HSBC, and Zoom.
They embedded malicious JavaScript in Optimizely to steal card details. The code also exposed older, unpatched iPhones and iPads to an exploit kit.
RELATED STORY: Cybersecurity in the Age of AI
Optimizely said that it has fixed the issue and removed the injected code in an update on November 17.

“Earlier today, Optimizely identified a security incident in which an unauthorized party exploited a vulnerability in Experimentation and used it to add malicious JavaScript to some customer projects.,” Optimizely wrote on their website.

“We’ve fixed the vulnerability and removed the injected code from affected projects. We’ve also taken steps to secure affected user accounts and put additional protections in place to prevent unauthorized code from being delivered.”
Today, Zoom announced that it has disabled Optimizely and has found no customer data to be compromised.

“Zoom is aware of the Optimizely security incident. As a precautionary measure, Zoom has disabled Optimizely across our production environments. At this time, we have not identified any impact to customer data. We continue to monitor the situation closely.”
Apple has yet to issue a statement regarding the attack.
